props.title: Process and catalyst for synthesis of methanol

props.name: copper, magnesia and silica (coprecipitated), Cu-MgO-SiO2
props.description: Coprecipitated from sodium silicate, magnesium nitrate and copper nitrate with sodium hydroxide; empirical composition after drying about 28.3 % CuO, 28.8 % MgO, 42.9 % SiO2, after reduction about 24 % Cu, 30.5 % MgO, 45.5 % SiO2. Not to be confused with copper deposited on asbestos.

evidence.quote: I have found that a catalyst mass compris ing copper, magnesia and silica gives surpris ingly better results, than either of these mate rials alone, or the copper and magnesia.
35. After drying the empirical composition of the catalyst was about 28.3% CuO, 28.8% MgO and 42.9% SiO,
After this reducing treatment the empirical composition of the catalyst was about 24% Cu, 30.5% MgO, and 45.5% SiO,
In this final form the catalyst is probably of a complex structure, as yet un known, but which I formulate as Cu-MgO-SiO, and call copper, magnesia and silica,

props.name: Cu-MgO-SiO2 better than components alone or Cu-MgO

evidence.quote: I have found that a catalyst mass compris ing copper, magnesia and silica gives surpris ingly better results, than either of these mate rials alone, or the copper and magnesia.

props.statement: A catalyst mass comprising copper, magnesia and silica gives surprisingly better results than either of these materials alone, or copper and magnesia.

props.name: copper up to 50 %, at least 5-10 %, best 25-30 % by weight

evidence.quote: I have found in general that these catalyst materials are valuable with proportions of copper running up to 50% by weight of the
If the per cent of metallic reduced copper is above this amount, I have found that the catalysts sin ter very easily and lose their effectiveness as methanol catalysts.
If the percentage of copper is less than 5 or 10% by weight of the catalyst mass, I have found that the rate of conver sion is not satisfactory.
I have found that in general approximately 25-30% by weight of metallic copper gives the best results.

props.statement: The catalysts are valuable with up to 50 % by weight copper; above this they sinter very easily and lose effectiveness; below 5 or 10 % the rate of conversion is not satisfactory; approximately 25-30 % by weight metallic copper gives the best results.

props.name: reduced granules hard and firm, suited to any synthesis system

evidence.quote: After reduction the granules were dark copper colored, and of a hard, firm, though brittle structure suited for any methanol syn thesis system.

props.statement: After reduction the granules were dark copper coloured and of a hard, firm though brittle structure suited for any methanol synthesis system.

props.name: any H2/CO ratio works; about 4:1 best, below 1:1 much lower S.T.Y.

evidence.quote: My catalyst will form methanol from a gas mixture having any ratio of hydrogen to carbon monoxide, but if the ratio is below one to one by volume the S.T.Y. will be con siderably lower
I have found that a gas containing about four volumes of hydro gen to each volume of carbon monoxide gives the best results, and that with about 6 vol umes of hydrogen the S. T.Y. is somewhat lower.
In general, I prefer not to use less hydrogen than that required theoretically by the equation 2H + CO = CHOH.

props.statement: The catalyst forms methanol from any ratio of hydrogen to carbon monoxide, but below one to one by volume the S.T.Y. is considerably lower; about four volumes hydrogen per volume CO gives the best results; with about 6 volumes the S.T.Y. is somewhat lower; preferably not less hydrogen than theoretically required and not over 6 volumes per volume CO.

props.name: MgO and SiO2 in equimolecular amounts form the balance

evidence.quote: that the MgO and SiO, present in equimolecular amounts.
the MgO and SiO, form the balance of the catalyst preferably in the proportions noted.

props.statement: The MgO and SiO2 are present in equimolecular amounts and form the balance of the catalyst, preferably in these proportions.

props.name: the coprecipitated catalyst is distinct from copper on asbestos

evidence.quote: However, this catalyst is not to be confused with one prepared by depositing copper on asbestos as a support.
My copper-magnesia-silica definition is accordingly to be applied only to my copre cipitated product, as herein described, and asbestos is disclaimed from this definition.

props.statement: The catalyst is not to be confused with copper deposited on asbestos; the copper-magnesia-silica definition applies only to the coprecipitated product, though it may be deposited on asbestos or another carrier.

props.name: use gas free from arsenic, sulphur, phosphorus, volatile iron compounds

evidence.quote: it is desirable to use gases substantially free from the common catalyst poisons which may be present in the raw materials, such as,
for example, arsenic, sulphur, phosphorous, volatile iron compounds, or other deleterious constituents gathered during the gas produc tion.

props.statement: For methanol synthesis with this catalyst the gases should be substantially free from the common catalyst poisons such as arsenic, sulphur, phosphorus, volatile iron compounds or other deleterious constituents.

props.name: methanol from 5 atm upward (even 1 atm), best 200-300 atm

evidence.quote: methanoi will be formed in substan tial amounts by this catalyst at pressures of 5 atmospheres and upwards, dependent on the temperature used.
Substantial yields of methanol may even be obtained at pressures lower than this; for example, at one atmos here.
In gen eral, I have found that the best results are secured between 200 and 300 atmospheres,

props.statement: Within these temperatures methanol is formed in substantial amounts at 5 atmospheres and upwards, and even at one atmosphere, though then the S.T.Y. is so much lower as to be uneconomical; the best results are between 200 and 300 atmospheres.
